name: tagline-options
expectations: The response presents between three and five distinct options
Every option names the rhetorical figure it uses (or states 'no figure, diction only')

No option uses a negative parallelism ('not just X, it's Y', 'more than just', 'not only X but Y'); a plain antithesis with both poles real ('X, not Y') is allowed only if both poles are claims the input supports
Every option is shorter than the input tagline (fewer words)

No option adds a claim absent from the input: no social-proof superlative ('leading', 'the only', 'number one', 'trusted by', a customer count), no characterization of the alternative or status quo the input does not make, and no mechanism turned into a guaranteed outcome
Any candidate treatment the response's own claim check finds to add a claim is withdrawn, not presented as an option with a caveat
The response recommends one option and gives a reason
